scope: R167 in-model verification of the bit-pattern safety check (465 audited calls)

equivalence.combined_with_r166: R166 tested 37 crafted and randomised cases including the shapes the model audits and found zero count mismatches; together the two rounds establish exact count equivalence for both counts, multiplicity included

the_median_paradox: the bit version has a worse median per call, 30.5 ms against 24.6 ms, yet a lower total, 4.808 s against 6.656 s per step, so the native implementation has a much heavier tail. Totals are what matter for step time.
corrected_expectation_for_step_time: R162 removed the audit and the step fell 2.87 s while the native check measured about 8.3 s of device time, a ratio near 0.35. Applied to the 1.85 s device saving this gives about 0.6 to 0.7 s of net step time, not the 1.5 to 2 s I suggested after R163.
status: correction complete; the speed benefit is modest but real and the equivalence is now proven twice
remaining_audit_cost: even with the bit version the checks still cost 4.808 s of device time per step, so the audit stays a contract-required cost. Cutting it further needs a fused single-pass kernel over the int16 view.
